subject: general
question: Identify the INCORRECT relation between power (P), Current(I), Resistance (R) and potential difference (V).
solution:
The correct answer is __**P = IR²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Option 4 (P = IR²)** is incorrect because it does not correctly represent the relationship between power (P), current (I), and resistance (R).
 
• The correct formulas are:
 
 
• **P = I²R** - Power is equal to the square of the current multiplied by the resistance.
 
• **P = V²/R** - Power is equal to the square of the voltage divided by the resistance.
 
• **P = VI** - Power is equal to the voltage multiplied by the current.
 
 
 
• In the incorrect formula **P = IR²**, the exponent on resistance (R) should not be squared when calculating power.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The power formulas are derived from Ohm's Law and the basic definition of electrical power.
 
• **Ohm's Law:** V = IR, which states that voltage (V) is the product of current (I) and resistance (R).
 
• By substituting Ohm's Law into the power formula P = VI, we get the other two correct formulas:
 
 
• Substitute V = IR into P = VI to get P = I(IR) = I²R.
 
• Substitute I = V/R into P = VI to get P = V(V/R) = V²/R.
